contract: A created backup is a zip holding absdatabase.sqlite, the metadata/items and metadata/authors trees and a details entry (id, key sqlite, createdAt, serverVersion); the id is YYYY-MM-DDTHHmm and the file <id>.audiobookshelf in the backup path; a create that exceeds maxBackupSize is aborted, removed and answered 500.
exceptions: force is not applicable: backup creation has no force or override mode; a create either writes one archive or aborts and removes it.

Applying an archive whose absdatabase.sqlite is not a readable SQLite database is not asserted: upstream v2.37.2 replaces the database and exits 1 after Database.reconnect rejects with SQLITE_NOTADB. The live server wins over the intended rejection.
Named Go tests remain assertion leads for the Go implementation; the scenario refs are the black-box proof.

invariants.contract: A created archive's entries are exactly absdatabase.sqlite, metadata-items/<item id>/... for every metadata/items folder, metadata-authors/... and details; details is four lines id, sqlite, createdAt, 2.37.2 and matches the listed id, createdAt and serverVersion; the filename is <id>.audiobookshelf and the path backups/<filename>.

The zipped absdatabase.sqlite is a readable SQLite snapshot of the live install at creation time: its libraries rows carry values written before the create and its user and libraryItems counts equal the running database.

The archive copies metadata/items and metadata/authors byte for byte: every metadata.json and cover.jpg entry equals the file on disk and an author marker written under metadata/authors is present with its content; no metadata/logs or backup files are archived.
A create that exceeds maxBackupSize answers 500, removes the partially written archive and its temporary sqlite file, adds no list entry and leaves the existing archives unchanged.
BackupManager.init creates the configured backup directory on demand and throws when it cannot, so the process exits nonzero instead of serving with an unusable backup path.
